data.title: Hewlett Packard Enterprise slides 11% after Evercore ISI downgrade
data.description:
Shares of Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE), an enterprise technology infrastructure company, tumbled almost 11% on Monday. The stock dropped $6.68 to close at $55.41 after Evercore ISI downgraded the stock to In-Line from Outperform, citing a more balanced risk/reward profile following a sharp run-up in the share price.

The decline came one session after HPE surged just over 12%, as the stock has seen choppy trading recently.

What Happened to Hewlett Packard Enterprise

Evercore ISI downgraded HPE to In-Line from Outperform today, arguing that following the stock's recent appreciation, the risk/reward had become more balanced. The firm retained a $65 price target and identified Juniper integration progress, margin improvement, and potential Helios-related demand as factors that could shift its view more positively. Read more

On September 2, the company reported non-GAAP EPS of $1.11 and revenue of $12.2 billion, both above consensus estimates. Management raised its fiscal 2027 revenue-growth framework to 13%–17% and projected at least $5 billion in free cash flow.

On the earnings call, management also flagged supply constraints involving memory and wafer capacity as expected to persist, and noted that gross margin should moderate toward historical levels as the Cloud & AI business mix increases. Read more

data.title: Intercont sets 25-for-1 reverse split to regain Nasdaq compliance
data.description:
• Intercont (Cayman) (NCT) announced on Monday that it will carry out a 25-for-1 reverse stock split effective September 17, 2026.
  • The move is aimed at restoring compliance with Nasdaq’s $1 minimum bid price requirement.
  • Starting September 17, the shares will trade on a split-adjusted basis under the same NCT ticker but with a new CUSIP.
  • Moreover, every 25 existing shares will become 1 share. The company’s issued Class A shares will fall from about 25.4M to 1.02M.
  • The shareholders do not need to take any action. Brokerage accounts will be adjusted automatically.

data.title: Veea and NovaGen plan $750M business combination
data.description:
• Veea (VEEA) and NovaGen Group signed a term sheet to combine, targeting a definitive business combination agreement within the coming weeks.
  • The companies will launch NovaGen Health Networks, combining Veea’s edge computing, connectivity and cybersecurity with NovaGen’s regenerative medicine platform, with initial deployments planned for Q4 2026.
  • GeoNova Capital has committed to invest $10M in the combined company as a cornerstone investor.
  • Management estimates the combined company could be valued at ~$750M, based on internal projections and an independent valuation.
  • The platform will initially connect health records, wearable data and biological measurements, with plans to expand into clinician-supervised diagnostics and therapy pathways subject to clinical validation and regulatory approvals.

data.title: J&J/Contineum depression candidate fails in phase 2
data.description:
• An asset for major depressive disorder licensed to Johnson & Johnson (JNJ) from Contineum Therapeutics (CTNM) missed its primary endpoint in a phase 2 trial.
  • In the MOONLIGHT-1 trial, JNJ-5120/PIPE-307 did not improve the Montgomery-Åsberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS) total score compared with placebo. 
  • J&J will continue to evaluate the data to determine next steps. 
  • JNJ-5120, an M1 muscarinic receptor antagonist, also failed a phase 2 trial for relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis in November 2025.

data.title: dLocals taps Oscilar to boost compliance workflows across 60+ markets
data.description:
• dLocal (DLO) announced on Monday that it has selected Oscilar to strengthen its compliance operations across 60+ markets and 1K+ payment methods.
  • Oscilar will support AML monitoring, sanctions screening, and investigations, with workflows tailored to different markets.
  • Its AI agents will help compliance teams review alerts and handle time-consuming tasks while human analysts keep final control over decisions.
  • The move is aimed at helping dLocal manage rising payment volumes and changing regulatory requirements without adding the same level of operational complexity.
  • Oscilar also provides audit trails and explainable decisions, giving dLocal greater visibility and control over its compliance processes.
